# Standard library: text, errors and I/O

Formatting, strings, numbers to text, errors, bytes and the io interfaces.

Listing of the hosted build (linux, amd64): every exported name, one line each, with the
ownership kind of each type (`value`, `view`, `owner (moves)`, `counted`; see section 8.7). Methods are
indented under their type. For the full comment of a name run `pluto doc pluto/strings Cut` or
`pluto doc pluto/vec Vec.Push`. `(*T)` is a pointer receiver (borrows); `(T)` on an owner type
consumes the receiver.

## pluto/fmt

Package fmt formats values, in the style of Go's fmt. Fprintf and Printf write to an io.Writer through a fixed buffer without allocating; Appendf, Append and Appendln append to a *vec.Vec[byte], which grows, or a *vec.Fixed[byte], which keeps what fits in a caller's array and never allocates; Sprintf, Sprint and Sprintln return a new string, allocated from the current allocator.

```
type ErrorBuf struct { _ unexported }  [view]
  // An ErrorBuf is storage for one formatted error, owned by whoever holds it: a parser, a device, a connection.
  func (b *ErrorBuf) Error() string
  func (b *ErrorBuf) Errorf(format string, args ...any) error
  func (b *ErrorBuf) Unwrap() error
type GoStringer interface { GoString() string }  [view]
  // A GoStringer has a GoString method used by %#v.
type Lister interface { FmtList() (first any, n int) }  [view]
  // A Lister is a container that formats as a list of its elements, like a slice: [a b c], or T{a, b, c} with %#v.
type Mapper interface { FmtSlots() int; FmtSlot(i int) (k, v any, ok bool) }  [view]
  // A Mapper is a container that formats like a Go map: map[k:v k:v] with its keys sorted, or T{k:v, k:v} with %#v.
type Stringer interface { String() string }  [view]
  // A Stringer has a String method used by %v and %s.
func Append[D vec.Appender[byte]](dst D, args ...any)
func Appendf[D vec.Appender[byte]](dst D, format string, args ...any)
func Appendln[D vec.Appender[byte]](dst D, args ...any)
func Errorf(format string, args ...any) error
func Fprint(w io.Writer, args ...any) (int, error)
func Fprintf(w io.Writer, format string, args ...any) (int, error)
func Fprintln(w io.Writer, args ...any) (int, error)
func Print(args ...any) (int, error)
func Printf(format string, args ...any) (int, error)
func Println(args ...any) (int, error)
func Sprint(args ...any) string
func Sprintf(format string, args ...any) string
func Sprintln(args ...any) string
```

## pluto/errors

Package errors implements functions to manipulate errors, as Go's errors package does, without allocating behind the caller's back.

```

func AsType[E error](err error) (E, bool)
func Is(err, target error) bool
func Join(errs ...error) error
func New(text string) error
func Unwrap(err error) error
```

## pluto/unicode/utf8

Package utf8 implements functions and constants to support text encoded in UTF-8. It mirrors Go's unicode/utf8. Nothing here allocates, except AppendRune into a growing vec.Vec: the byte slice functions view their argument as a string without copying.

```
const: MaxRune, RuneError, RuneSelf, UTFMax
```

## pluto/bytes

Package bytes implements functions for the manipulation of byte slices, mirroring Go's bytes package where that is possible without allocating. Functions that return part of their argument return a subslice of it, not a copy. Buffer is Go's growing buffer, with storage from an allocator.
